task_name: Deploy relay and E2E happy path

strengths: Deploy compose is isolated per spec infra constraint: dedicated named network 'agentpair-net', dedicated 'relay-data' volume, and explicit 127.0.0.1:3001:3001 loopback bind — no kareema container/network references anywhere (deploy/school-compose.yml:1-19, docker-compose.yml:1-19), satisfying the must-not-have and scoped rollback via 'docker compose down'.
Dockerfile uses node:22-bookworm-slim (debian-slim, not alpine) with python3/make/g++ for better-sqlite3 native build, exactly matching spec §Dependencies note (packages/relay/Dockerfile:2-6).

start.ts binds 0.0.0.0 inside the container while host publish is loopback-only, correctly reconciling container reachability with the '127.0.0.1:3001 only' spec constraint (packages/relay/src/start.ts:13).

dual-server.ts cleanly models the full §8 happy path in-process (pair -> approve -> bonded -> session_open -> challenge -> test_reports -> sign -> ratify -> closed) over real HttpRelayClient transport, with clear step-by-step error diagnostics and envelope dedup via WeakMap (packages/mcp-server/src/e2e/dual-server.ts:162-347).
Test asserts behavior not just execution: co-signed hash equals artifact hash, thread present, and both ratify pendings cleared after finalize (packages/mcp-server/src/e2e/happy-path.test.ts:39-46).

issues.description: docker-compose.yml and deploy/school-compose.yml are byte-for-byte identical. Both are mandated deliverables in the plan, but keeping two identical copies risks drift between local-dev and school-deploy configs; consider having one reference the other or documenting the divergence intent.

The test instantiates two MCP server instances (aliceMcp/bobMcp) but only asserts they are defined; the actual happy-path flow runs through separately-constructed agent contexts from createDualAgent rather than being dispatched through those MCP server instances. Relay transport is genuinely exercised, so the deliverable is met, but the 'two in-process MCP instances' aspect is superficial.

Dockerfile has no HEALTHCHECK directive and runs the relay as root; a HEALTHCHECK would strengthen the '/health returns 200' verification and a non-root USER is a container hardening best practice. Neither is required by the quality bar.
